seed_ranking.label: Robertson--Sanders--Seymour--Thomas (1996/1997)
seed_ranking.inclusion_reason: The target explicitly presents RSST as the simpler proof and quadratic-time algorithmic baseline that this paper improves from additive-constant reduction to constant-factor reduction.

seed_ranking.label: Steinberger (2010)
seed_ranking.inclusion_reason: The target says it uses exactly Steinberger's discharging rules and that theorem (i) is a more specific version of Steinberger's positive-charge theorem.

seed_ranking.label: Franklin (1922)
seed_ranking.inclusion_reason: The target uses Franklin as a precursor for obstructing-cycle reduction and as the source of the classic 6-regular configuration that is not D-reducible.

seed_ranking.label: Birkhoff (1913)
seed_ranking.inclusion_reason: The target cites Birkhoff for internal 6-connectivity of minimal counterexamples and for the Birkhoff diamond as a D-reducible configuration.

seed_ranking.label: Appel--Haken (1976/1977; 1989 book form)
seed_ranking.inclusion_reason: The target uses Appel--Haken as the earlier reducibility-based proof benchmark and contrasts its own stronger linear-many objective against that older scale.

pressure_points: Earlier proofs and algorithms yield only one reducible configuration or obstructing cycle at a time, so recursion shrinks the problem by an additive constant and total time remains quadratic.
Classical discharging explains positive-curvature regions but not the flat zero-curvature regions the target wants to exploit.
The target needs D-reducible configurations that can be used many times simultaneously, not just a single classical witness.
missing_cell_analysis: No ancestor paper body beyond the target itself was read.
All ancestor descriptions are target-mediated rather than independently verified from the ancestor papers.
The run supports first-hop genealogy only and does not support second-hop edges among ancestor papers.

transferred: Reducible-configuration and obstructing-cycle reduction as the overall four-color proof template.
Steinberger's discharging rules and positive-final-charge implication.
Franklin's obstructing-cycle reduction and Birkhoff's D-reducible diamond / internal-6-connectivity framing.
novel: Linearly many pairwise non-touching reducible configurations or non-crossing obstructing cycles.
Use of flat zero-curvature regions rather than only positive-curvature neighborhoods.
Near-linear O(n log n) four coloring.
A larger D-reducible 6-regular configuration for the flat case.
unsupported_stronger_claims: Older papers already contained the target theorem in disguised form.
The target's novelty is only implementation detail.

blind_reconstruction: The paper begins from the classical reducible-configuration/obstructing-cycle framework, treats RSST's quadratic algorithm as the immediate baseline, imports Steinberger's positive-charge discharging machinery, and then pushes beyond the one-reduction-at-a-time regime by extracting many local reductions in flat regions.
comparison_with_target: The reconstruction matches the target's explicit move from additive-constant to constant-factor shrinkage.
It matches the target's explicit statement that theorem (i) reuses Steinberger's framework while theorem (ii) and (iii) are the fundamental new contributions.
It remains deliberately weaker than any deeper historical reconstruction that would require reading the ancestor papers themselves.
reconstructed_question: How can the classical four-color reducibility-and-obstruction framework be strengthened so that planar triangulations yield linearly many simultaneously usable local reductions, including in flat zero-curvature regions, thereby supporting near-linear-time four coloring instead of quadratic-time additive-constant recursion?

confidence_and_uncertainty.summary: A cautious full first-hop genealogy is supported by direct target-text evidence, but all non-target historical claims remain target-mediated because ancestor-paper bodies were not read.
uncertainties: No independent reading of RSST, Steinberger, Franklin, Birkhoff, or Appel--Haken paper bodies.
No justified second-hop genealogy among the ancestor papers.
